_comment: CELPIP Reading Part 2: Reading to Apply a Diagram. The diagram is a table; an email with 5 blanks must be completed from it, then 3 questions about the email.

items.title: Fall fitness classes
items.instructions: Read the following schedule and the email that refers to it.

passage.title: Lakeview Community Centre: Fall Fitness Classes
rows: In the pool; bring a swimsuit
notes: Lakeview residents get 15% off all paid classes.
Register at the front desk or online by September 5.

tasks.intro: Read the email. Complete it by choosing the best option for each blank, using the schedule.
tasks.text:
Hi Rosa,

I just looked at the fall class schedule at the community centre, and I think I've found the right classes for us. Since you've never done yoga before, I think you should try {{1}}. It's on Tuesday evenings, so it won't interfere with your Saturday shifts at the bakery. And you won't need to buy anything because {{2}}.

I'm going to sign up for Aqua Fit. It costs {{3}} for ten weeks, which is a little more than your class, but I like that it meets twice a week. I'd love to try the spin class too, but it's on {{4}} mornings, and I usually visit my mother then.

Don't forget that we both live in Lakeview, so we'll get {{5}} off. We need to register by September 5, so let's go to the front desk together this weekend.

Talk soon,
Leila

questions.explanation: Yoga Basics is the beginner yoga class on Tuesdays.
The notes for Yoga Basics say mats are provided.
Aqua Fit costs $90 for 10 weeks.
Spin Class is on Saturday at 9:00 a.m.
Lakeview residents get 15% off all paid classes.

tasks.intro: Choose the best option for each question about the email.

questions.prompt: Why does Leila think Yoga Basics is right for Rosa?
options: Rosa has done yoga for years.
Rosa is a beginner and works on Saturdays.
questions.explanation: Rosa has never done yoga, and the Tuesday class does not conflict with her Saturday shifts.

questions.prompt: Why will Leila not take the spin class?
options: It is at a time when she visits her mother.
It is only for advanced students.
questions.explanation: 'It's on Saturday mornings, and I usually visit my mother then.'

questions.prompt: What does Leila suggest they do this weekend?
options: Register together at the front desk
questions.explanation: 'Let's go to the front desk together this weekend.'

items.title: Choosing a moving company
items.instructions: Read the following comparison and the email that refers to it.

passage.title: Moving company quotes: two-bedroom apartment, 40 km
notes: Moves on Saturdays and Sundays cost 10% more.

tasks.intro: Read the email. Complete it by choosing the best option for each blank, using the comparison.
tasks.text:
Hi Marco,

I've been comparing quotes from moving companies for our move on June 30. Since we have to be out of the apartment that day, we can't use {{1}}, because they can't come until July 3, even though they have the best reviews.

Two Guys & a Van is the cheapest, but they don't offer {{2}}, and I'm worried about your piano. QuickMove's insurance only goes up to {{3}}, which isn't enough for all our things.

I think Northern Relocation is the best choice. Their price is $1,450, and we can pack everything ourselves to avoid paying {{4}} for packing. The only problem is that June 30 is a Sunday, so the price will be {{5}} higher.

Let me know what you think, and I'll call them tomorrow.

Ana

questions.explanation: Maple Movers' earliest date is July 3, and it has the best rating (4.8).
Two Guys & a Van has no insurance, which matters for an expensive piano.
QuickMove's insurance covers up to $5,000.
Northern Relocation charges an extra $300 for packing.
Moves on weekends cost 10% more.

tasks.intro: Choose the best option for each question about the email.

questions.prompt: Why is Ana writing to Marco?
options: To ask him to pack the piano
To change the date of their move
questions.explanation: She compares the companies and recommends Northern Relocation.

questions.prompt: What worries Ana about Two Guys & a Van?
questions.explanation: They offer no insurance, and she is worried about the piano.

questions.prompt: What will Ana probably do tomorrow?
questions.explanation: 'I'll call them tomorrow', meaning Northern Relocation.

items.title: Summer day camps
items.instructions: Read the following list of camps and the email that refers to it.

passage.title: Riverside Parks and Recreation: Summer Day Camps
rows: Outdoors in Riverside Park; bring a lunch
Before-care from 8 a.m. for $25 a week
notes: Families registering two or more children save $20 per child per week.

tasks.intro: Read the email. Complete it by choosing the best option for each blank, using the list of camps.
meta: Subject: Summer camps for the kids
tasks.text:
Hi Tom,

I've been looking at summer camps for the kids. Ella is turning 10 in June, so she's too old for Nature Explorers, but she'd love {{1}}. She's always asking to help in the kitchen. It's only in the mornings, though, so we'd need a plan for the afternoons.

For Noah, I think Sports Mix is perfect. He's 7, and the camp runs until {{2}}, which works with my schedule. Since I start work at 8:30, we'd also need to pay {{3}} a week for before-care.

If we register both kids, we'll save {{4}} per child each week. Both camps run from July 14 to {{5}}, so let's choose weeks in that period.

What do you think?
Mira

questions.explanation: Junior Chefs is a cooking camp for ages 8–12.
Sports Mix runs from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
Before-care costs $25 a week.
Families with two or more children save $20 per child per week.
Junior Chefs ends on August 8, so both camps overlap from July 14 to August 8.

tasks.intro: Choose the best option for each question about the email.

questions.prompt: Why does Mira think Ella would enjoy Junior Chefs?
options: Ella wants to be with Noah.
questions.explanation: 'She's always asking to help in the kitchen.'

questions.prompt: What problem does Mira mention about Junior Chefs?
options: It does not cover the afternoons.
Ella is too young for it.
It starts too late in July.
questions.explanation: 'It's only in the mornings, though, so we'd need a plan for the afternoons.'

The camp is far from their home.
Mira starts work before the camp begins.
